finding.title: Verify emailVerified (or the invite_token) before granting tutor-invite acceptance by email match

evidence.quote: // This prevents anyone from claiming an invite not addressed to them.
// without needing the emailed deep link. Match the caller's verified email.

finding.why: Firebase Auth lets anyone register an account with any unverified email string. acceptTutorInvite, declineTutorInvite, and listTutorGrants({mode:'pending_for_me'}) all authorize 'is this caller the invited tutor' purely by comparing the caller's Auth email to grant.tutor_email -- none of them checks callerRecord.emailVerified (or the token claim), despite comments at both call sites explicitly (and incorrectly) claiming this 'prevents anyone from claiming an invite not addressed to them' / matches the 'verified' email. An attacker who front-runs registration of the invited tutor's email address can call listTutorGrants(pending_for_me) to discover the grantId, then acceptTutorInvite to gain ongoing read access (and any write permissions the parent granted) to the child's full learning profile -- without ever proving ownership of that inbox. The invite_token generated specifically to prevent exactly this (comment: 'single-use, per NFR-3') is stored on the grant doc but is never read back or compared anywhere in the file, so it provides zero actual protection. cf_grant_invite.test.mjs's own header comment confirms this exact gate is never exercised by any test.
finding.recommendation: Require callerRecord.emailVerified === true in acceptTutorInvite/declineTutorInvite before trusting the email match, and/or require the caller to supply invite_token and compare it against grant.invite_token (the mechanism already built for this). Apply the same emailVerified gate to listTutorGrants' pending_for_me query so an unverified account cannot even discover invites addressed to an email it doesn't own.
acceptance_criteria: A new Auth-emulator-backed test in cf_grant_invite.test.mjs seeds an unverified-email account and asserts acceptTutorInvite rejects it (e.g. permission-denied).
acceptTutorInvite/declineTutorInvite check emailVerified or invite_token before authorizing by email match.
make test-functions (or a new CI job per the companion finding) seeds Auth-emulator users so this path is actually exercised, not skipped.
